preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain ownership)
Attacker must hold some 1SHIBA tokens to demonstrate fee impact

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setTaxFeePercent() and setLiquidityFeePercent() with extremely high values (e.g., 99). Then perform token transfers to trigger fee collection. The high fees will cause significant token deductions from users, with portions converted to BNB and sent to the marketing address (which the owner could control) or added to liquidity where the owner receives LP tokens. The owner can also exclude themselves from fees using excludeFromFee() to avoid paying the high fees.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract implements a reflection token with tax and liquidity fees. The owner has privileged functions to set fee percentages up to 99%. When fees are collected, part is converted to BNB for liquidity and LP tokens are minted to the owner. By setting extremely high fees and excluding themselves from fees, the owner can drain value from users through transfers.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Become owner via storage slot manipulation. 2. Set tax and liquidity fees to 99% each. 3. Exclude attacker address from fees. 4. Fund a victim account with tokens. 5. Trigger victim transfer to collect high fees. 6. LP tokens are minted to owner (attacker), increasing their value.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Find owner storage slot (slot 0 in Ownable). 2. Use vm.store() to set owner to attacker. 3. Impersonate owner to call setTaxFeePercent(99) and setLiquidityFeePercent(99). 4. Call excludeFromFee(attacker). 5. Create victim account and give it tokens. 6. Make victim transfer tokens to trigger fee collection. 7. LP tokens are minted to attacker (owner).

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract is a reflection token where owner can set fees up to 100%. By setting high fees and excluding themselves, the owner can drain value from users. Fees are partially converted to LP tokens sent to owner.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Become owner via storage slot 0 overwrite. 2. Set high but reasonable fees (30% each). 3. Exclude attacker from fees. 4. Create victim with tokens via storage manipulation. 5. Trigger victim transfer to collect fees and mint LP tokens to owner.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Overwrite owner slot to become owner. 2. Set taxFee and liquidityFee to 30%. 3. Exclude attacker from fees. 4. Find storage slot for victim's rOwned balance and set it. 5. Make victim transfer to trigger fee collection. 6. LP tokens minted to attacker.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: We need a simpler approach. Instead of complex storage manipulation, we can impersonate the actual owner to transfer tokens to victim. But we don't have the owner's private key. Alternative: Use deal() cheatcode to give victim tokens? deal() works for ERC20 tokens. But this is a reflection token, so deal() might not work correctly. Better: We can become owner and then use the contract's own functions to give tokens.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Become owner via storage slot 0. 2. Set reasonable fees (20% each). 3. Exclude attacker from fees. 4. Use owner's balance to transfer tokens to victim (owner should have tokens from deployment). 5. Make victim transfer to trigger fee collection.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Overwrite owner slot. 2. Set fees to 20%. 3. Exclude attacker. 4. Transfer tokens from owner to victim using transfer() function. 5. Make victim transfer to trigger fees.
